sentences.text: This animal features broad, belt-like armor plates in the middle of its back that display grooves and holes forming radial designs.
The side plates possess large horns that sweep backward, a feature also seen in related typothoracines such as Typothorax.
A distinct knob covers the back edge of every single armor plate.
This animal was a widely distributed aetosaur found in Germany, North America, and possibly parts of Gondwana.
Paratypothorax is an extinct genus of aetosaur containing only one known species, Paratypothorax andressorum.
The first specimens were collected in the Heslach area near Stuttgart, Germany.
Although the best specimens come from Germany, they were wrongly thought to be phytosaur armor for over a century.
The holotype specimen, SMNS 5721, includes connected osteoderms along with some hip and leg bones.
It was first recognized as an aetosaur in 1953 and formally named as a new genus in 1985.
Fossils were first identified in the Chinle Group of the southwestern United States in 1992.
A complete skeleton, specimen SMNS 19003, was unearthed in 1945 from the Schlipf Quarry near Murrhardt.
Paratypothorax was a large, wide-bodied typothoracine aetosaur and serves as the namesake for the tribe Paratypothoracisini.
It is classified within the family Stagonolepididae.
Paratypothorax belongs to the tribe Paratypothoracisini.
The fossil range of Paratypothorax is estimated to be from the Late Carnian to the Rhaetian.
The formations in the southwestern United States where Paratypothorax was found date to the Carnian and Rhaetian stages of the Late Triassic.
Paratypothorax lived during the Norian stage, approximately 227.3 to 205.7 million years ago.
Fossils have been found in the Sonsela Member of Petrified Forest National Park in Arizona and the Bluewater Creek Formation in western New Mexico.
Osteoderms have been reported from the Norian-age Fleming Fjord Formation in Greenland, the Zarzaitine Series in Algeria, and an unverified site in India.
